subtopic: ONNX IR version vs opset version
learningObjective: Distinguish the ONNX IR (file format) version from the operator opset version, and identify a common source of load-time incompatibility.
stem: A user tries to load an ONNX file and gets an error about unsupported version. Which distinction between the ONNX **IR version** and the **opset version** best explains the diagnostic they should perform?

options.text: IR version and opset version are synonyms in ONNX; the diagnostic is to check `model.ir_version` and upgrade the consumer if it differs by more than 1.

The IR version governs the model file/graph format (how ModelProto, GraphProto, NodeProto are laid out); the opset version governs operator semantics. A load-time incompatibility can come from either — the consumer's ONNX library too old to parse the IR, or too old to know the declared opset — so the diagnostic must inspect both fields in `model.ir_version` and `model.opset_import`.

The opset version is a lower bound on IR version and always exactly one greater; the diagnostic is therefore to update the opset by +1 and re-export the model, which is guaranteed to resolve any version error.
IR version is only used for training checkpoints; inference models omit IR version entirely, so the diagnostic is to check whether the file was accidentally saved as a training checkpoint.

explanation: ONNX distinguishes the IR version (`ir_version`, versioning of the model protobuf format itself) from the opset version (`opset_import[i].version`, versioning of the operator schema library). Both evolve independently; a mismatch on either can make a model unloadable. The correct diagnostic looks at both. Options A/B/C fabricate relationships that do not exist in the ONNX spec.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: IR version and opset version are separate axes.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: two-axis versioning per the ONNX specification.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: no such exact relationship exists.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: IR version is present on all ONNX models.

assumptions: The file is a well-formed ONNX protobuf.
nonImplications: Does not imply every version mismatch is fatal; some ORT versions can be forward-compatible within an opset range.
Does not imply upgrading ONNX always fixes the issue; some old runtimes are the constraint.
